title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They use threats to scare you into acting quickly.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be suspended unless you confirm your Social Security number right now."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Medicare or Social Security number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link to fix it. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please update your address here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Requests for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Do not click the link—delete the message and check with the delivery company using their official website or phone number.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from Social Security, saying there’s a problem with your account. They ask you to click a link or call a number to fix it, but it’s really a trick to steal your information.
example_message: "We noticed suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please verify your information by clicking this link."
red_flags: Email says there’s a problem with your account
Asks you to click a link or call a number
what_to_do: Do not click any links—go to the official Social Security website or call their real number to check your account.

title: Facebook 'Friend in Need' Money Request
how_it_works: A scammer hacks a friend’s Facebook account and sends you a message saying they’re in trouble and need money. They ask you to send money quickly, often by gift card or wire transfer.
example_message: "Hi, I’m stuck and need your help. Can you send me a $200 gift card right away?"
red_flags: Urgent request for money from a friend
Asked to send gift cards or wire money
Message seems out of character for your friend
what_to_do: Call your friend directly using a number you know to check if the request is real.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a number for help. The scammer on the phone asks for remote access to your computer or payment for fake repairs.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now: 1-800-XXX-XXXX"
red_flags: Pop-up says you have a virus
Asked to call a phone number
Asked to give remote access or pay for repairs
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number—if you’re worried, contact a trusted local computer repair shop.
